items.title: Joe Ascione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: You talk to all these great drummers, Simon Phillips and Dennis James and I’m friends with Carly Euder and all these guys and we sit there and talk

ctx.x: I’m part time faculty at the New School for Jazz down in Manhattan. So I have a handful of students there and some private students. I know a lot of professional players who want to come in and work on some technique or work on this or work on that. First I ask them what their goals are and what they’re looking to do, and then I kind of make a quick

assessment. I’m a good troubleshooter teacher, if I do say so myself. But I’ll sit there and check out a drummer and catch his vibe and see the playing and see if his goals match his style. You know if he’s coming in and flipping sticks and bashing drums and double bass riffs, I doubt he’s going to be playing in a little quiet jazz trio. He might want to try that because he digs it, but even Charlie Watts now he’s playing jazz because he made a trillion dollars with the Stones and now he’s doing what he —…
Yeah. That’s a hard thing to do but you’re not doing them any favors by not doing it.
